label: Completing Square

label: Completing Square
text: Introduction

label: Completing Square
text: What is Completing Square?

label: Completing Square
text: A quadratic expression with form ax² + bx + c can be rewritten in the form of a(x − h)² + k, which we name this process as "Completing Square".

label: Completing Square
text: For example, x² + 4x + 5 = (x + 2)² + 1.

label: Completing Square
text: Type 1 — Leading Coefficient as 1

label: Completing Square
text: Quadratic expressions in the form x² + bx + c

label: Completing Square
text: Divide the coefficient of x (i.e. b) by 2 to obtain the value of h in the form of (x + h)² + k. e.g. For x² + 4x + 5, h = 4/2 = 2, i.e. (x + 2)² + k e.g. For x² − 6x − 3, h = −6/2 = −3, i.e. (x + (−3))² + k

label: Completing Square
text: Divide the coefficient of x (i.e. b) by 2 to obtain the value of h in the form of (x + h)² + k.

label: Completing Square
text: Add the term (b/2)² (you may neglect the negative sign), and subtract back (b/2)² such that x² + bx + (b/2)² form a perfect square. e.g. x² + 4x + 5 = x² + 4x + (2)² − (2)² + 5 e.g. x² − 6x − 3 = x² − 6x + (3)² − (3)² − 3

label: Completing Square
text: Add the term (b/2)² (you may neglect the negative sign), and subtract back (b/2)² such that x² + bx + (b/2)² form a perfect square.

label: Completing Square
text: Simplify the residue expression (−(b/2)² + c). e.g. x² + 4x + 5 = (x + 2)² − 4 + 5 = (x + 2)² + 1 e.g. x² − 6x − 3 = (x − 3)² − 9 − 3 = (x − 3)² − 12

label: Completing Square
text: Simplify the residue expression (−(b/2)² + c).

label: Completing Square
text: Type 2 — Leading Coefficient in Forms of Non-1

label: Completing Square
text: Quadratic expressions in the form ax² + bx + c

label: Completing Square
text: Take out the factor a for the terms ax² and bx; ignore the constant term c. e.g. −x² + 4x + 8 = −(x² − 4x) + 8 e.g. 3x² + 6x − 1 = 3(x² + 2x) − 1

label: Completing Square
text: Take out the factor a for the terms ax² and bx; ignore the constant term c.

label: Completing Square
text: Add and subtract the term (b/2)² such that x² + bx + (b/2)² inside the bracket form a perfect square. e.g. −x² + 4x + 8 = −(x² − 4x + (2)² − (2)²) + 8 e.g. 3x² + 6x − 1 = 3(x² + 2x + (1)² − (1)²) − 1

label: Completing Square
text: Add and subtract the term (b/2)² such that x² + bx + (b/2)² inside the bracket form a perfect square.

label: Completing Square
text: Simplify the residue expression by −a(b/2)² + c; be careful on dealing with brackets. e.g. −x² + 4x + 8 = −(x² − 4x + 4) + 4 + 8 = −(x − 2)² + 12 e.g. 3x² + 6x − 1 = 3(x² + 2x + 1) − 3 − 1 = 3(x + 1)² − 4

label: Completing Square
text: Simplify the residue expression by −a(b/2)² + c; be careful on dealing with brackets.

label: Quadratic Functions
text: A quadratic function has 3 different forms which show different geometric features of its graph (a parabola).

label: Quadratic Functions
text: Type 1 — General Form y = ax² + bx + c

label: Quadratic Functions
text: Coefficients and their roles

label: Quadratic Functions
text: Coefficient a determines 1) Direction of opening and 2) Wideness of the parabola.

label: Quadratic Functions
text: If a < 0, the parabola will open downward.

label: Quadratic Functions
text: If a > 0, the parabola will open upward.

label: Quadratic Functions
text: The larger |a| is, the narrower the opening gets.

label: Quadratic Functions
text: Coefficient c determines the y-intercept of the parabola.

label: Quadratic Functions
text: By substituting x = 0 to the quadratic equation, the value of y is always equal to the constant c.

label: Quadratic Functions
text: Coefficient b determines the axis of symmetry of the parabola.

label: Quadratic Functions
text: The axis of symmetry is a vertical line that passes through the vertex of the parabola and lies exactly midway between the two x-intercepts (if they exist).

label: Quadratic Functions
text: Equation of the axis of symmetry is x = −b/(2a) (x-coordinate of the vertex).

label: Quadratic Functions
text: Type 2 — Vertex Form y = a(x − h)² + k

label: Quadratic Functions
text: Geometric features from vertex form

label: Quadratic Functions
text: By converting the General Form y = ax² + bx + c into the Vertex Form y = a(x − h)² + k, we can directly identify the critical geometric features of the parabola:

label: Quadratic Functions
text: Coordinates of the vertex: (h, k), which is the lowest point (for a > 0) or the highest point (for a < 0).

label: Quadratic Functions
text: Equation of the axis of symmetry: the vertical line x = h.

label: Quadratic Functions
text: Minimum value k (for a > 0) or maximum value k (for a < 0) of y.

label: Quadratic Functions
text: Two methods to find the vertex

label: Quadratic Functions
text: 1. Method of completing square

label: Quadratic Functions
text: 2. By substitution

label: Quadratic Functions
text: By comparing the two forms, h = −b/(2a). Since we know that the axis of symmetry passes through the vertex as well, we can find the value of k by substituting the value of h into x after computation.

text: Two points A(a, m) and B(b, n)

label: Coordinate Geometry
text: Slopes of Lines

label: Coordinate Geometry
text: Four cases of slope

label: Coordinate Geometry
text: Case 1: if (m − n)/(a − b) > 0, it is upward sloping.

label: Coordinate Geometry
text: Case 2: if (m − n)/(a − b) < 0, it is downward sloping.

label: Coordinate Geometry
text: Case 3: if m = n (y-coordinate equal), (m − n)/(a − b) = 0 and it is a horizontal line.

label: Coordinate Geometry
text: Case 4: if a = b (x-coordinate equal), (m − n)/(a − b) is undefined and it is a vertical line.

label: Coordinate Geometry
text: Two lines with slopes p and q

label: Coordinate Geometry
text: Case 1: if p = q, the two lines are parallel to each other.

label: Coordinate Geometry
text: Case 2: if p × q = −1, the two lines are perpendicular to each other.

label: Coordinate Geometry
text: The previous cases are not including situations when at least one of the lines are vertical lines.

label: Glossary
text: Glossary of Key Terms

label: Glossary
text: Every definition from the notes, in one place.

label: Glossary
text: Discriminant (Δ)

label: Glossary
text: The expression Δ = b² − 4ac for a quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0.

label: Glossary
text: Completing Square

label: Glossary
text: Rewriting a quadratic expression ax² + bx + c in the form a(x − h)² + k.

label: Glossary
text: Sum of roots

label: Glossary
text: For ax² + bx + c = 0, α + β = −b/a.

label: Glossary
text: Product of roots

label: Glossary
text: For ax² + bx + c = 0, αβ = c/a.

label: Glossary
text: Complex number

label: Glossary
text: A number of the form a + bi, where a and b are real numbers and i = √(−1).

label: Glossary
text: Conjugate

label: Glossary
text: The conjugate of a + bi is a − bi.

label: Glossary
text: General form (quadratic)

label: Glossary
text: y = ax² + bx + c. Shows opening, axis of symmetry and y-intercept.

label: Glossary
text: Vertex form (quadratic)

label: Glossary
text: y = a(x − h)² + k. Shows vertex (h, k) and axis of symmetry x = h.

label: Glossary
text: Intercept form (quadratic)

label: Glossary
text: y = a(x − α)(x − β). Shows x-intercepts α and β.

label: Glossary
text: Axis of symmetry

label: Glossary
text: A vertical line that passes through the vertex of the parabola and lies exactly midway between the two x-intercepts (if they exist). Equation: x = −b/(2a).

label: Glossary
text: Centroid (G)

label: Glossary
text: The point where the three medians of a triangle meet. Always lies inside the triangle. Coordinates: ((x_a + x_b + x_c)/3, (y_a + y_b + y_c)/3). AG : GD = 2 : 1.

label: Glossary
text: Orthocenter (H)

label: Glossary
text: The point where the three altitudes of a triangle meet. Inside for acute, at the right-angle vertex for right-angled, outside for obtuse.

label: Glossary
text: Circumcenter (O)

label: Glossary
text: The center of the circumscribed circle, formed by the intersection of the perpendicular bisectors. OA = OB = OC (radii).

label: Glossary
text: Incenter (I)

label: Glossary
text: The center of the inscribed circle, formed by the intersection of the angle bisectors. DI = EI = FI (radii). pr = 2A. Coordinates: ((ax_a + bx_b + cx_c)/(a + b + c), (ay_a + by_b + cy_c)/(a + b + c)).

label: Glossary
text: Euler's line

label: Glossary
text: For all triangles, the circumcenter O, the centroid V and the orthocenter H lie on the same line.

label: Glossary
text: Perpendicular Bisector Property

label: Glossary
text: If PQ is a perpendicular bisector of BC, then any points on PQ can form isosceles sides with BC (e.g. PB = PC and OB = OC).

label: Glossary
text: Angle Bisector Property

label: Glossary
text: If BI is an angle bisector of ABC with AB ⊥ DI and BC ⊥ IF, then DI = IF.

label: Glossary
text: Angle Bisector Theorem

label: Glossary
text: BM/MC = AB/AC, similarly for other two pairs.

label: Glossary
text: i (imaginary unit)
